rationale: PLP likely failed due to a consent/locale gate and dynamic, late-rendered product grid. Adding OneTrust accept handling, broader grid wait selectors, and robust product tile/link selectors increases the chance of materializing the PLP. Normalizing and persisting locale/country parameters prevents redirection to unsupported locales (e.g., en-jp) or corporate domains. PDP price fallbacks via schema.org meta ensure price extraction even if visual selectors differ.
code_hints: Handle cookie/CMP gate: if element #onetrust-accept-btn-handler is present, click it before PLP waits.

After navigation, wait for any of: [main [data-testid*='plp'], ul[class*='product-grid'], .product-list]; then perform incremental auto-scroll to bottom with short delays (e.g., 300–500ms) until no new tiles for 2 cycles.

If no product tiles after 6–8s, retry once after clicking potential locale/region confirmations: button:has-text('Continue'), button:has-text('United Kingdom'), [data-testid='close-button'], button[aria-label='Close'].
When extracting PDP price, fall back to meta[itemprop='price']@content if visible spans are missing; also read currency from meta[itemprop='priceCurrency']@content when available.
Preserve and propagate query params forceLocale=en-int&shipToCountry=GB on all in-site links to avoid locale traps; when following PLP -> PDP links, append missing params.
Use a realistic desktop Chrome UA with Accept-Language: en-GB,en;q=0.9 and enable stealth to reduce bot challenges.
Guard against soft 204/JS-only render: wait for document.readyState >= 'interactive' and a MutationObserver for up to 8–10s to detect late-rendered tiles.
